scene: A glossy 3D-rendered supermarket with blue glass walls sits at the centre of a model city made of plain white-grey blocks. A neon-yellow band wraps the facade at mid height and an orange-bordered sign with an ALDI wordmark and logo mark hangs above the entrance. No people or headline text appear.
mechanism: The title leaves the store unnamed, and the image answers with one lit, branded building floating in a blank city, so the 'unassuming' store is turned into a glowing subject.
composition: The ALDI sign is the secondary point, set high on the central tower of the building.
typography: There is no headline; the only letters are the ALDI wordmark on the sign, about a tenth of the frame wide. At 160x90 that wordmark falls to a few pixels, so all text work is left to the title.
colors: Saturated cobalt blue and neon yellow-orange on a near-monochrome white and light grey city, with a dark navy fade across the top edge. The glow on the glass and ground makes the store pop from its surroundings.
psychology: Without any figure the frame leans on a single lit object in a pale field, which signals importance and quiet scale rather than emotion. Nothing in the image reads as danger, fear or urgency.
partnership: The title withholds which store it means and the thumbnail names it through the sign, so the image supplies the missing noun. The 'quietly changing America' claim is not pictured, which keeps the question of how open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glowing blue building first, then the yellow neon band along the facade, then the ALDI sign, with the white blocks last.
art: Clean render with soft contact shadows, consistent perspective and a depth-of-field blur toward the corners. The blocky city is deliberately simple, so the frame stays uncluttered, but the store interior is only suggested through lit windows.
strength: One saturated object isolated in a neutral city gives instant subject separation without any text.
weakness: The only identifying cue, the ALDI sign, is small, and the frame has no face, number or headline to hold a viewer.
bottleneck: At phone size the store reads as a generic blue shop, because the wordmark that tells the viewer which store this is shrinks to a smudge.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the sign to roughly a quarter of the frame width, or add a short overlay beside the store, and compare recognition at 160x90 against this version.
mechanism_secondary: single lit object in a neutral model city
counterexample: Seq 22 carries a three-line headline and a stressed face on white, where this frame has no text or person at all.
hero_object: glowing ALDI store in white model city
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A faceless white mannequin-style head sits on a body in a brown tweed jacket and red-and-blue tartan shirt, and a white-gloved hand draws a fine brush across a framed portrait. The gilded frame holds a painted man in an olive military-style jacket and tie with side-parted dark hair and a small square moustache. A short hand-drawn yellow arrow at the upper left sweeps up toward the blank head.
mechanism: The blank-faced painter beside a finished portrait turns 'fooled' into a picture of someone anonymous deceiving a regime, and the headline states the claim outright.
composition: The mannequin figure occupies the left 40 percent and the gilded frame the right half, with the brush bridging the two. The two-line headline sits at the lower left over the tweed jacket, and the dark vignette pushes attention to the pale head and the lit portrait.
typography: Two stacked lines of heavy condensed capitals: HE FOOLED in white and EVERY NAZI in yellow, about a fifth of the frame tall, with a dark shadow behind. Both lines stay legible at 160x90. The wording restates the title with 'he' replacing 'the painter who' and adds no new fact.
colors: Near-black ground with warm gold on the frame, the yellow headline and the yellow arrow, plus the white of the head and glove as the brightest points. The olive and brown tones of the portrait and jacket keep the palette muted and period-like.
psychology: The blank face removes any expression, so the cue is the stern, level gaze of the painted portrait and the steady brush hand. The image carries tension through the subject matter rather than through a visible emotion.
partnership: The text is nearly the title reworded and the image only illustrates it, so no new information is introduced. The picture does pose the question of who the faceless painter is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white blank head first, then the portrait face in the frame, then the headline at the lower left, with the yellow arrow noticed last.
art: Photoreal render with a dramatic side-lit spotlight and consistent shadows on the frame, glove and jacket. The brush reaches the portrait's chin plausibly. The glossy blank head is the one stylised element.
strength: The mannequin head beside a portrait is a clear one-glance image of an anonymous painter at work.
weakness: The yellow arrow is small and points at the blank head without saying why, so its role is unclear.
bottleneck: Headline and picture repeat the title's claim without adding a specific detail, so the frame depends on the viewer already finding 'fooled every Nazi' interesting.
action: Hypothesis: replace the arrow with a short added clue, such as a brushstroke detail or a year, to test whether a new fact adds more than the repeated headline.
mechanism_secondary: faceless forger beside a portrait
counterexample: Seq 21 pairs a title-restating idea with two labelled faces in conflict, where this frame has only one faceless figure.
expression_label: blank mannequin head; stern painted portrait
hero_object: gilded framed portrait and mannequin painter
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SENIORS MUST KNOW THIS! / IF YOU ARE 70, 80 OR 90 YEARS OLD / DO THIS SIMPLE / MOVEMENT! [name tag: Dr. Momadian Doctor] [duration badge: 24:15]
scene: A woman with long wavy dark hair in dark-green scrubs points a finger toward the headline with her raised hand and gives a closed-mouth smile at the viewer. A white name tag on her chest reads Dr. Momadian Doctor. Four text blocks sit on a dark-blue gradient, with a teal strip across the top and a 24:15 duration badge at the lower right. No exercise or movement is pictured.
mechanism: A stack of age-callout and imperative lines with a pointing clinician sells an unnamed 'simple movement' for anyone in their seventies or beyond, so the action stays hidden.
composition: The headline fills the left two thirds as four stacked blocks and the woman is cropped at the right edge, about a third of the width. Her pointing arm cuts back toward the text, which links figure and copy, but the four text bands of different styles compete as anchors.
typography: Seventeen headline words across four bands: white capitals on a teal strip, large white capitals, then yellow capitals on two teal boxes. All four lines read at 160x90, though the middle one is smaller than the yellow bottom pair. The name tag and the badge text vanish at that size. The text drops the title's walking problem and adds the 'simple movement' fix.
colors: Dark navy gradient with white and highlighter-yellow capitals and bright cyan-teal boxes, so contrast is very high. The green scrubs sit close in value to the navy background and the figure separates mainly through her skin and hair. Yellow is used for emphasis here, not as an alarm tone.
psychology: The smile is composed and the finger points straight at the age line, which reads as friendly address in a teacher-like pose. The age numbers and 'must know' phrasing carry the urgency; her face does not.
partnership: The title names a walking problem and an unnamed 'real fix', and the thumbnail replaces the problem with an age call-out and a 'simple movement'. The unanswered question is which movement, which keeps the reveal intact.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the top strip SENIORS MUST KNOW THIS first, then the large white age line, then the yellow DO THIS SIMPLE MOVEMENT boxes, then the woman's face and pointing hand.
art: Smooth, evenly lit portrait with an uncluttered gradient ground and a cut-out edge that stays clean around her hair. The figure is rendered in a glossy, polished style, and the gradient plus flat text boxes give a templated look.
strength: Naming three ages at once makes the target viewer obvious and gives the promised movement a clear audience.
weakness: Four competing text bands leave the woman small and cropped, and nothing pictures the movement itself.
bottleneck: The headline and the title talk about different things, walking versus a movement, so the thumbnail dilutes the specific problem the title opens with.
action: Hypothesis: cut the top strip and the age list to one line, and add a small image of the movement being done, to test whether a visible action lifts the story.
mechanism_secondary: age call-out with unnamed simple movement
counterexample: Seq 16 uses the same teal-and-clinician layout with far fewer words, where this frame stacks four text bands.
hero_object: pointing doctor beside DO THIS SIMPLE MOVEMENT boxes
medical_notes: The title and thumbnail promise a fix through one 'simple movement' with no stated basis, and the printed name tag (Dr. Momadian) differs from the channel name Dr. Aliza Wright, so the clinician's identity and credentials cannot be confirmed from packaging.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: Stolen Life [lost LEGACY logo, top left]
scene: A cartoon woman with a large halo of dark curly hair and turquoise drop earrings cries, with blue tears running down both cheeks, a furrowed brow and a downturned mouth. She wears a cream puff-sleeved dress with gold vertical stripes, and her clasped hands are bound in grey iron shackles with a chain hanging below. A thin black curved arrow beneath the hand-lettered words points back toward her on a plain white background.
mechanism: A single weeping, shackled figure and a two-word label turn a second-person title into an image of what was taken from someone, so the viewer sees the loss before the story.
composition: She fills the left 45 percent of the frame and is cropped at the waist, with the chained hands at the bottom edge
typography: about an eighth of the frame tall
colors: Warm browns, cream and gold on pure white, with turquoise earrings and pale blue tears as the only cool accents. The white ground gives maximum separation for the dark skin tones and black linework.
psychology: a downturned open mouth showing teeth
partnership: The title promises a first-person 'your life' story and the thumbnail gives a verdict, stolen, with a crying face. It adds an emotional framing without naming a place, date or event.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the tearful face first, then the shackled wrists, then the handwritten Stolen Life, with the arrow and small corner logo last.
art: Clean digital illustration with solid colour fills, a consistent outline weight and confident highlights on skin and fabric. The white background keeps it uncluttered; the corner logo is a small wordmark in thin lines.
strength: Tears, shackles and a two-word label state the emotional premise in under a second against a clean white ground.
weakness: The right half is mostly empty space and the thin lettering is lighter than the figure, so the text feels undersized.
bottleneck: The thin hand-lettered words sit far from the face, and at small size the arrow and the logo are noise rather than guidance.
action: Hypothesis: set Stolen Life in a heavier weight and move it closer to the face to test whether a bolder, nearer label strengthens the first read.
mechanism_secondary: sympathy through tears and shackles
counterexample: Seq 5 uses an angry mob and a loud yellow headline for a historical topic, where this frame uses a single tearful figure and quiet text.

scene: A big-headed cartoon figure with tangled brown hair, wide round eyes glancing sideways and a flat frown wears a ragged fur tunic in the lower left foreground. Behind him five smaller figures in similar fur wraps scowl with angled brows, and four of them stretch an arm toward him. The setting is a dusk valley with rocky cliffs, a crescent moon and thatched huts at the right.
mechanism: An accused figure in front and a pointing mob behind picture the question of punishment before any method is named, and the question mark leaves the answer open.
composition: The large head at lower left is the primary focal point and the five small figures in a diagonal line behind him are secondary, so the pointing arms converge on the head. The headline spans the whole top edge, and the huts and moon at the right fill the remaining space without competing.
typography: Two words in yellow capitals with a dark outline, about a sixth of the frame tall, across the full width. Readability at 160x90 is high. The words compress the title into a short question and add no fact it lacks.
colors: A purple-blue dusk sky and grey-brown ground with a yellow headline as the brightest element. The pale faces of the figures stand out against the dim blue-grey, and the brown fur tunics share the ground's tone.
psychology: The foreground face shows wide eyes looking aside and a flat mouth, a worried or uneasy look, while the crowd shows frowning brows and open mouths. Together they read as accusation against a lone figure.
partnership: The title asks how ancient humans punished criminals, and the thumbnail shows the accused and his accusers with the same question in two words. The image adds the scene of the mob and withholds any method, so the answer stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow PUNISHED HOW? first, then the big worried face, then the pointing crowd, with the huts and moon last.
art: Hand-drawn stick-figure style with simple circular heads and a painted, textured background. Proportions are consistent between characters, though the foreground head is oversized relative to the crowd, as intended. The gradient sky is clean.
strength: The lone worried face against a pointing mob is an instantly readable accusation scene.
weakness: The headline format and flat-yellow styling resemble several other history thumbnails in this batch, so little marks this one apart.
bottleneck: The question mark and yellow banner are the same device used across channels in this batch, which limits how distinct the frame looks in a feed.
action: Hypothesis: replace 'PUNISHED HOW?' with a concrete, unusual penalty drawn as an object in the accused's hands to test whether specificity beats the generic question.
mechanism_secondary: lone accused figure versus pointing mob
counterexample: Seq 24 puts one puzzled figure opposite a row of sad cave dwellers, where this frame places the lone figure under a crowd's accusation.
hero_object: worried accused figure and pointing crowd
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: VIEWS 1,000,000,000 / SUBSCRIBERS 10,000,000 / REVENUE $4,200,000 [YouTube on the two wall plaques]
scene: A cartoon youth with a brown fringe, round glasses and a black hoodie grips his head with both hands, eyes wide and mouth open. Three white cards across the top show VIEWS 1,000,000,000, SUBSCRIBERS 10,000,000 and REVENUE $4,200,000 with small icons. Behind him hang a silver and a gold play-button plaque and two framed certificates. Banknotes float through the room, a jar of notes and coins stands on the desk, and a laptop shows a rising bar chart with an upward arrow.
mechanism: Three oversized counters and a shouting face dramatise the title's 'finally go viral' with numbers so extreme that the scene reads as a fantasy payoff.
composition: The figure sits dead centre under three cards that run the full width, so the layout is symmetrical and the face is the main focal point. The cash jar at lower left and the laptop at lower right frame him, and the floating notes fill the sides.
typography: Six figures and labels across three cards, each number in bold black on white, with the numbers about a tenth of the frame tall. At 160x90 the cards survive as white boxes but the digits shrink to a few pixels and cannot be read. The numbers add specifics the title does not contain.
colors: Beige and tan walls with muted green banknotes, a black hoodie and white cards as the highest-contrast elements. Colour is low in saturation overall, and the figure stands out through the dark hoodie against the light wall.
psychology: Wide round eyes, an open mouth and hands pressed to the head are an exaggerated shock or disbelief cue. The scene signals excitement through the flying cash rather than fear.
partnership: The title promises a viral-success scenario, and the thumbnail escalates it with exact billion-view, ten-million-subscriber and multi-million-dollar figures. The numbers answer 'how big' while leaving the method unmentioned.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the screaming face first, then the three stat cards across the top, then the cash jar and floating notes, with the laptop chart last.
art: Clean cartoon illustration with a consistent outline, a flat wall and soft shading on the notes and jar. Objects are coherent, and the card text is crisp. The many props make the scene busier than a face-and-text layout.
strength: A single shocked face under three large counters tells the viral-success story with numbers before any words.
weakness: The digits are unreadable at phone scale and the room is filled with props, so the cards read as grey boxes.
bottleneck: The numbers carry the proof of 'viral', and they shrink below legibility at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: keep one card with one large figure, for example the view count alone, and remove the plaques to test whether a single readable number lifts the frame at small size.
mechanism_secondary: extreme numbers with a shocked face
counterexample: Seq 5 uses a two-word headline and no numbers, which survives 160x90 where this frame's figures do not.
expression_label: wide eyes, open mouth, hands on head
hero_object: shocked creator with three stat cards

scene: A cartoon man with a navy baseball cap and a calm flat-mouthed face sits alone at a plain table in an office break room, opening a white lunch container. Behind him on the left, four colleagues walk past, three of them carrying paper takeaway bags and two holding paper coffee cups. The room has a bulletin board with pinned papers, a microwave and a fluorescent ceiling light.
mechanism: The solitary man with a packed lunch beside colleagues carrying takeaway turns a money habit into a scene of quiet difference, with no words needed.
composition: The cap man sits right of centre at about a third of the frame width and is the primary subject. The group at the left walks in the opposite direction, which sets up a left-right contrast, and the bulletin board between them anchors the middle of the frame.
typography: No text appears anywhere in the frame, so the title carries every word. Nothing needs to survive at 160x90 except the picture itself.
colors: Cool blue-grey walls, navy shirts and cap with warm tan table and bags, and soft warm window light at the right edge. Saturation is low to moderate, and no single colour is dominant.
psychology: The seated man's brows are slightly lifted and the mouth is a neutral line, while the colleagues smile while chatting. The contrast between a neutral expression and cheerful group sets up a left-out cue, although the face itself shows no strong feeling.
partnership: The title promises a life after thinking like old money, and the image shows a packed lunch beside others' takeaway, which suggests frugal habits but never names wealth or money. The viewer must connect the lunch scene to the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the cap-wearing man first, then the lunch container in his hands, then the group with takeaway bags at the left, with the bulletin board last.
art: Soft flat-colour cartoon with simple faces and clean outlines, but the source image is only 360x202 and looks soft and compressed. The leftmost person is cropped at the edge, and at small size the lunch container and bags are indistinct.
strength: A lone man with a packed lunch beside bag-carrying colleagues sets up a relatable contrast with no text.
weakness: The lunch box and the takeaway bags that carry the story are small and low in contrast, and the frame has no headline.
bottleneck: At 160x90 the key props blur, so the viewer sees a man at a table and a crowd without the meal cue that explains the scene.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the lunch container and one takeaway bag, or add a three-word label, to test whether the money cue becomes legible at feed size.
mechanism_secondary: packed lunch versus takeaway contrast
counterexample: Seq 11 states its contrast with a bold NO and a speech bubble, where this frame leaves the contrast entirely implicit.
expression_label: neutral flat mouth with raised brows

Beside him a bearded man with glasses in dark navy scrubs tilts his head with an open palm raised, as if speaking.
mechanism: Two symptom words in red and white over a clutching, grimacing man put a recognisable heart-attack image on the question without stating a diagnosis.
composition: The usable image covers only about a third of the frame width, with the headline across its top and the two faces in the lower half. The red chest glow at the lower centre is a third focal point, and the blurred brown bars on either side hold no content.
typography: Two bold condensed lines: PAIN + in white and SWEAT? in red, each about a seventh of the frame tall, inside the narrow centre panel. The words read at 160x90 but at small width, and the pillarboxed layout leaves roughly two thirds of the frame empty. The text names two symptoms the title only implies as 'warning signs'.
colors: Black-to-navy centre panel with a red glow at the left, red SWEAT? and white PAIN, set between warm brown blurred bars. The red chest glow and red word act as danger signals against the dark ground.
psychology: Furrowed brow, shut eyes, grimace and a hand pressed to the chest are explicit distress cues, and the second man's tilted head and open palm read as explanatory concern. Red signals urgency.
partnership: The title gives age, an urgency line and 'warning signs', while the thumbnail names two concrete signs in a question. The two together raise the stakes without giving away which signs the video covers.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white PAIN and red SWEAT? first, then the grimacing man's face, then the glowing chest and hand, then the bearded man.
art: Photoreal studio-style portrait with consistent dark lighting and a clean red glow on the shirt. The glow is a stylised graphic overlay. The blurred side bars are enlarged copies of the image's own colours and add no content.
strength: The red-glow hand on the chest is a clear symptom picture, and PAIN + SWEAT? names the symptoms in two words.
weakness: Pillarboxing wastes about two thirds of the frame, so the faces and headline are small in a 16:9 tile.

action: Hypothesis: crop the vertical art to fill a 16:9 tile, with the symptom words at the same relative size, to test whether a larger face and headline improve the first read.

counterexample: Seq 18 uses the same pillarbox format with a challenge word rather than symptoms, where this frame names the symptoms outright.

text: YOU MUST / KNOW THIS ABOUT / LOSARTAN & / AMLODIPINE
scene: An illustrated older man with swept-back grey hair and thin-framed glasses smiles with his mouth open and tips a clear glass of water to his lips with one hand. His other hand holds a small white pill between thumb and finger at chest height. He wears a pink collared shirt, and the black background carries four lines of headline text at the left.
mechanism: Two prescription drug names under a 'you must know' lead, with a man swallowing a pill, make the unstated warning feel specific to people who take these medicines.
composition: Four text lines fill the left 60 percent and the man occupies the right 40 percent, cropped at the waist, with his head near the top edge. The pill and the glass sit close to the centre line, so the eye travels from the headline across to the pill.
typography: Seven words in four lines: yellow capitals for YOU MUST and KNOW THIS ABOUT, white LOSARTAN &, and white AMLODIPINE reversed out of a red box. Each line is large and legible at 160x90, with the drug names given the heaviest emphasis. The title adds a third drug and the blood-pressure context that the thumbnail omits.
colors: Pure black ground, saturated yellow and white text, a red label box and a hot-pink shirt as the warm centre of the figure. Contrast is extreme and the pink shirt separates the figure from the black, so the frame reads as an alert.
psychology: The man's open smile and relaxed raised glass signal ease while the text says he must know something, so the image and the headline give mixed cues. The red box on the second drug name adds an alarm tone that the face does not share.
partnership: The thumbnail repeats the title's 'must know' phrasing and two of its three drug names, so it mostly duplicates and drops the blood-pressure context. What the viewer is supposed to know is left unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow YOU MUST first, then the red AMLODIPINE box, then the man's face and glass, then the pill in his hand.
art: Digital illustration with a textured, painted look and visible hatching on the shirt and skin. The hand holding the pill is small and slightly crude, and the figure is cleanly cut out against the black.
strength: Naming two exact drugs in large type targets a specific viewer at a glance.
weakness: The smiling pill-taker undercuts the warning tone, and the pill itself is tiny against the headline.
bottleneck: The headline never says what about the drugs matters, so the red box signals alarm without giving the viewer a reason beyond the brand names.
action: Hypothesis: add one concrete concern word beside the drug names, for example a short symptom or interaction label, to test whether specificity beats the generic 'must know' lead.
mechanism_secondary: named prescription drugs with an unstated caution
counterexample: Seq 13 uses the same black, yellow and red layout with an older woman eating, but its text states a quantity, 4 eggs, where this frame names drugs with no figure.
hero_object: pill and water glass with drug names
medical_notes: The packaging names two prescription blood-pressure drugs with a 'you must know' alert but states no content, so the implied risk or interaction cannot be judged from the title and image alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon Greek warrior with a headband, beard and gold scale armour pulls a bow with gritted teeth at the left edge. A one-eyed white giant with a black beard and a blue eye bares his teeth at the right, one fist clenched and a wooden club on his shoulder, and sheep crowd the lower right. A blue sea map with red looping route lines spreads across a tan background behind both.
mechanism: Two famous opposing characters, a map and a runtime stamp pack the whole epic into one image, and the number frames the video as a quick summary.
composition: The warrior and the giant bookend the frame, with the headline running across the middle between them. The bow line and the giant's club push the eye inward to the text. The map fills the entire background and gives the layout a busy, even texture.
typography: Five words across two lines in thick white capitals with a heavy black outline: THE ODYSSEY in a larger size and IN 13 MINUTES below. Both lines read at 160x90 over the busy map, though the black outline carries most of the contrast. The runtime is a detail that the title does not state.
colors: Sea blue and tan with red route lines, gold armour and the white bodies of the two characters. The outlined white text sits against mid-tone colours, so its contrast comes from the outline rather than the ground.
psychology: The archer shows clenched teeth and a narrowed eye while the giant shows bared teeth and a glaring single eye, so both read as aggression. The sheep and the club add a comic note.
partnership: The title promises the entire story explained, and the thumbnail adds a thirteen-minute length and two recognisable story figures. It reveals the characters but not the plot, so the promise stays intact.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large white THE ODYSSEY first, then the giant's single eye, then the archer at the left, then IN 13 MINUTES and the map.
art: Bold-outline cartoon with flat colour and white highlights on armour and muscle. The character edges overlap the text zone without hiding the letters, and the background map is detailed enough to add clutter at small size.
strength: The two opposed characters and the runtime give the viewer a fast, concrete sense of what is inside.
weakness: The map with its looping red routes sits directly behind the lettering and adds visual noise to the headline.
bottleneck: The letters sit across the characters' bodies and the map at once, so the headline competes with the busiest part of the frame.
action: Hypothesis: place the title on a solid or darkened band across the middle to test whether removing the map noise makes the runtime stand out more.
mechanism_secondary: runtime stamp over two story characters
counterexample: Seq 12 shows one calm figure on a simple desert background, where this frame stacks two characters and a map.
expression_label: gritted teeth and glaring one-eyed snarl
hero_object: archer and one-eyed giant with map

text: Beer o'clock? You in? / NO [wall calendar: OCTOBER 2026]
scene: A woman in a green blouse and glasses waves a hand with a ring while speaking, and a yellow-outlined speech bubble above her reads Beer o'clock? You in?. Beside her a man in a blue shirt stands and a woman in a cream blouse claps. In the right foreground a cartoon man in a navy cap with a flat mouth and level brows sits at a computer, with a yellow NO above him and a red curved arrow pointing down at him. Seven smaller coworkers work at desks in the background, and a wall calendar reads OCTOBER 2026.
mechanism: A social invitation from three smiling coworkers is met with a single yellow NO, so the frame dramatises refusing a spend-related offer in a workplace.
composition: The three inviting coworkers fill the left third and the cap man sits right of centre, so the layout splits into 'asked' and 'refuses'. The NO at upper right and the red arrow close the triangle by pointing at the cap man's head. The office behind adds depth, but keeps the frame crowded.
typography: The bubble holds two short mixed-case lines whose letters fall to roughly 5 pixels tall at 160x90 and do not read there. NO is large yellow capitals about a seventh of the frame tall and is the one element that survives at small size. The only digits are on a prop calendar. The text never mentions pay, payday or a formula from the title.
colors: Warm office beige, blue shirts and a green blouse with yellow as the only text colour and a red arrow as the accent. The yellow bubble outline and the NO share one hue, which links invitation and refusal.
psychology: The coworkers show open smiles, a clapping gesture and a raised hand, a cheerful social-pressure cue, while the cap man's flat mouth and level brows read as unmoved. The red arrow marks him as the one to watch.
partnership: The title tells the viewer to do something every time they get paid, and the thumbnail shows turning down a drinks invitation. The refusal is a spending-restraint image, but pay and the formula in the title are not pictured.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow NO first, then the cap man's face, then the smiling group and the speech bubble, with the red arrow and calendar last.
art: Polished cartoon with consistent outline weight and soft interior shading. The cap man's blank round face contrasts with the detailed expressive faces of the coworkers, and the many people and desk items make the scene dense.
strength: A single yellow NO against a cheerful group makes the refusal obvious at first glance.
weakness: The speech bubble's small text and eleven figures crowd the scene, and the title's payday idea never appears.
bottleneck: The only readable word at 160x90 is NO, and it refuses something the viewer cannot see, so the story depends on the unreadable bubble.

text: IS MEMORY / LOSS NORMAL / WITH AGING? [logo: Helping Older Parents]
scene: The same smiling woman with dark curly hair, gold drop earrings, a white coat, a maroon blouse and a blue stethoscope appears in a rounded photo at the right of a flat teal field. At the lower left a thin-line circular logo shows two walking figures, one with a cane, above the words Helping Older Parents. The headline fills the upper left.
mechanism: A plain question about memory loss with a clinician photo and a family-care logo turns the title into a familiar, reassuring explainer card.
composition: Stacked headline text fills the left half, the portrait fills the right, and the logo sits at the lower left, which makes a balanced three-part layout. The face at upper right is the focal point and the headline the second.
typography: Six headline words in three large lines of black capitals, with NORMAL set in white as the only emphasis, plus the three-word logo caption. The headline is much larger than the text in the paired falls thumbnail and reads at 160x90, while the logo caption does not. It repeats the first half of the title and adds nothing beyond it.
colors: A flat mid-turquoise ground with black and white text and the maroon, white and navy of the portrait. The white NORMAL has less contrast than the black words, but the larger type keeps it readable.
psychology: The relaxed closed-mouth smile and the direct gaze read as calm reassurance, which fits a question about a worrying topic. No visible cue signals fear or urgency.
partnership: The title asks whether memory loss is normal in aging and mentions helping older parents in a podcast, and the thumbnail copies the question and adds the logo. It gives no answer, so the open question is the only hook.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large black IS MEMORY LOSS first, then the white NORMAL, then the woman's face, with the logo last.
art: Studio-lit portrait with a soft blurred street background set in a rounded frame on a flat colour block. The logo is a fine line drawing and the layout looks templated rather than composited.
strength: A large three-line question on a plain background reads at once and names the topic without jargon.
weakness: The frame is a template: the same portrait and colours appear on other thumbnails from this channel, so nothing marks this topic.
bottleneck: The question has no emotional or specific detail, so the card relies entirely on the viewer already worrying about memory loss.
action: Hypothesis: replace the logo area with one visible concrete example, for example a short everyday forgetting scenario, to test whether specificity beats the generic question.
mechanism_secondary: reassuring clinician with a normal-or-not question

medical_notes: The title and thumbnail pose a neutral question about normal aging with a clinician portrait and a care-organisation logo, and make no cure or diagnosis claim.

scene: At the left five hunched cartoon prehistoric humans in fur wraps stand in a line with drooping faces and downcast eyes, each with a different look: a bearded man, a small child-sized figure in spotted fur, a dark-skinned figure in green rags, and a bald stooped one. At the right a stick-style man with brown hair and a fur tunic scratches his head with a raised hand and a puzzled look. A cave mouth and a starry night sky form the setting.
mechanism: One puzzled survivor facing a row of sad, different human types makes the title's 'only human species left' a lonely scene, and the headline asks it as a question.
composition: The five-person line runs across the left and middle and the single figure stands alone at the right, so the frame splits into many versus one. The headline sits at the top centre and the dark cave wall gives a low-key backdrop.
typography: Two words in large mustard-yellow capitals at the top centre, about a fifth of the frame tall and clearly readable at 160x90. WHY US? is the shortest headline in the batch and adds an emotional register that the title lacks.
colors: Dark grey-brown cave and blue-black night with warm fur browns and a mustard headline. The low-key tones make the headline the brightest element, and the pale faces of the figures are the second brightest.
psychology: The row shows drooping brows, downcast eyes and slumped shoulders, a sadness cue, while the lone figure's scratching hand and tilted head read as confusion. Together they show loss without any threat.
partnership: The title asks why we are the only human species left, and the thumbnail shows the sad others and the one survivor asking 'why us'. It supplies the emotional frame and leaves the biological reason unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow WHY US? first, then the puzzled figure at the right, then the row of sad faces from left to right.
art: Detailed hand-drawn cartoon with textured fur, shaded faces and a painted cave, while the survivor has a simple stick-style head. The mix of styles is consistent, and the dark scene stays clear at small size.
strength: A single puzzled figure facing five distinct, sad figures tells the 'last one standing' story at a glance.
weakness: The five sad figures are dark and similar in tone to the cave wall, so their individual faces disappear at small size.
bottleneck: The row of faces is the story, yet at 160x90 the five figures merge into one brown mass and only the headline and the survivor read.
action: Hypothesis: lighten the background behind the five figures or reduce them to three to test whether the faces stay distinct at 160x90.
mechanism_secondary: lone survivor versus a row of sad human types
counterexample: Seq 5 puts one worried figure under a pointing crowd, where this frame places a puzzled figure opposite a quiet, sad row.
